sources.entry: Dropserver - An application platform for your personal web services. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Go/Deno

summary.one_liner: Dropserver is an application platform for running your own personal web services, written mainly in Go with Deno as the sandbox for app code.
summary.what_it_does: Builds two executables: ds-host, a complete server that runs apps in appspaces and responds to requests directed at them (Linux/x86_64 only), and ds-dev, a local tool for developing Dropserver apps (Linux and Mac). App code runs inside Deno sandboxes, and Deno must be installed separately. The README says users can upload app code, create appspaces, migrate, add users, and share an appspace with other users. The repo also contains a Vue 3 frontend for each executable and a checkinject utility for verifying injected Go dependencies. The author organizes the Go code into many small packages with interface-based dependency injection.
use_cases: Hosting personal web services on a home server or cloud VM
Developing and testing Dropserver apps locally
Running small multi-user web apps for friends or family
Sandboxing untrusted app code with Deno
how_to_run: Install Deno separately, since it is not packaged with the Dropserver executables
Build ds-host and ds-dev from the repository (the README points to the GitHub Actions release workflow as the best guide to build steps)
Follow the dropserver.org docs: 'Using ds-dev' for local development
Follow the dropserver.org docs: 'Run your own Dropserver with ds-host' for server deployment
notable: Two executables: ds-host for servers and ds-dev for local app development
App code runs in Deno sandboxes
Go code organized as many small packages with interface-based dependency injection
checkinject utility to verify required dependencies are non-nil
caveats: The README warns that Dropserver is intended to run untrusted code and that security is not claimed to be solid; it advises against exposing it to the public internet unless isolated in a VM
Known goroutine and memory leaks, some missing or half-baked functionality, and app APIs expected to change
ds-host runs only on Linux/x86_64; Deno must be installed separately
keywords: run apps on my home server
